notes: Example configuration generated by the CraneCalc configurator; fictitious crane, supplier, survey and owner data, to be replaced with project data. Scope: 6 simply supported 35-ft bays, W21X111 girders, one 3-ton cab crane, on new welded twin-rib bracket seats welded to the existing W14X90 columns, with the rail, ties, bearings and end stops; the existing columns are checked with their existing load effects and the existing sidewall rod bracing takes the crane longitudinal forces. A direct flange saddle does not suit this rolled girder (the sized saddle leaves saddle-across-fatigue 0.97 for the estimated tie demands; a welded saddle is a Category D/E attachment on the top flange of this high-cycle runway (CMAA Class C, AIST Class B)): the tie is paired flat bars, which bolt to the tie-side bearing stiffener, cut as one plate with its gusset extension past the flange tip (no weld at the gusset), the full-depth stiffener pair carrying the tie force into the girder. Bumper overhang assumed 20 in (end-wheel centerline to the extended bumper face, a typical supplier proportion): the stop contact positions use it; confirm with the crane supplier.

aist.cycleSource: Fictitious example duty: 500,000 crane passages in three duty bins (rated, half and light lifts), loaded and empty passes included. The bins are an assumed general-service proportion, not crane or owner data, so the fatigue checks govern by the all-cycle bound (the full fatigue load at every one of the 500,000 cycles); Miner's sum over the bins is listed for comparison until a sourced duty spectrum is entered.

Lightest compact W within the sizing targets (ratio ≤ 0.85, deflections ≤ 0.9 of the limits): screening estimates, top-flange tip stress (DG7, warping and second-order twist) ratio 0.73, vertical deflection 0.64, lateral 0.41 and rail-head movement with twist 0.55 of their limits; flanges at least 8.5 in wide for the end bearing bolt gauge and the rail seat; lighter candidates rejected: 27 by sizing ratio, 42 by flange width; the next lighter, W30X108: tips ratio 2.40 > 0.85; rail-head movement with twist 1.04 of the limit > 0.9. These are the configurator's screening estimates (a simplified model that ranks the catalog), not the final ratios: the calculation checks the section and reports its own ratios.

fabrication.steel: Girder ASTM A992; plates, bars and stiffeners ASTM A572 Grade 50 unless noted.
fabrication.bolting: ASTM F3125 Grade A325, pretensioned, Class B faying surfaces, standard holes unless slots are detailed. Sliding-end bearing bolts and column-end tie bolts pretensioned against steel sleeves. Rail joints thermite or flash-butt welded by the rail supplier's qualified procedure (preheat, grinding, inspection); no joint bars or bolts.
fabrication.welding: E70XX low-hydrogen electrodes per AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020, cyclically loaded provisions. Continuous fillets as dimensioned; no intermittent welds on cyclic load paths. Smooth starts and stops.
fabrication.inspection: Visual inspection of all welds; AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020 cyclically loaded acceptance criteria; magnetic particle testing of fillets at fatigue-sensitive attachments; 100% ultrasonic testing of CJP welds; bolt pretension verification per RCSC.
fabrication.erection: Set and level the bearings, install the end bearings and flange ties, then set the rails. Provide temporary restraint until the permanent ties are complete.
fabrication.railAlignment: Set the rails to the specified gauge, alignment and level tolerances and survey them after erection, before the load test.
